Precision concerns sampling uncertainty under the analysis; it does not remove bias. Evidence excluding a large effect need not exclude a smaller one, and an unresolved effect is neither evidence of benefit nor proof of exactly zero effect. Equivalence testing asks whether an effect lies within justified lower and upper bounds, preferably specified before seeing results, using an appropriate analysis. Non-inferiority instead asks whether a treatment is worse than its comparator by more than a prespecified margin. Neither question is settled by failing to reject a zero difference, and meaningful margins depend on the outcome and setting.
